actors.name: Administrator
actors.description: Manages users, doctors, departments, wards/beds and system configuration; views reports and the audit trail; may approve discharge overrides.

actors.name: Receptionist
actors.description: Registers patients, books/reschedules/cancels appointments, checks patients in (queue tokens), admits patients, allocates/transfers beds and completes discharge.

actors.name: Doctor
actors.description: Works through own queue, records consultations, writes prescriptions, orders lab tests, views patient history and lab results, requests admission/discharge.

actors.name: Lab Technician
actors.description: Processes lab test orders: records sample collection and enters results.

actors.name: Pharmacist
actors.description: Maintains medicine inventory, receives stock alerts and dispenses prescriptions.

actors.name: Billing Staff
actors.description: Generates invoices from unbilled charges, applies discounts, records payments and prints receipts; clears patients for discharge.

functional.text: The system shall authenticate users with a username and password and issue a session token valid for 8 hours.
The system shall lock an account for 15 minutes after 5 consecutive failed login attempts and shall reject logins for deactivated accounts.

The system shall restrict every operation according to the role-permission matrix (Administrator, Receptionist, Doctor, Lab Technician, Pharmacist, Billing Staff) and show each role only its permitted menus.
The system shall allow a logged-in user to log out and shall reject requests carrying a missing, invalid or expired token.
The Administrator shall be able to create user accounts with a unique username, full name, role and initial password (minimum 8 characters).
The Administrator shall be able to activate/deactivate user accounts and reset passwords; an Administrator cannot deactivate their own account.
The Receptionist shall be able to register a patient; the system shall generate a unique patient ID in the format P00001.
The system shall validate patient data: first and last name required, 10-digit mobile number, date of birth not in the future, valid gender and blood group values.

The system shall warn about a possible duplicate registration when a patient with the same mobile number and date of birth, or the same full name and date of birth, already exists; the Receptionist may confirm and proceed.
Authorised users shall be able to search patients by patient ID, name or mobile number.
The Receptionist shall be able to update patient demographic and contact details; the patient ID shall never change.
The system shall display a patient's history: appointments, consultations, prescriptions, lab results, admissions and invoices (clinical items only to clinical roles).
The Administrator shall be able to manage doctor profiles: department, specialisation, qualification, consultation fee, working days and hours, slot length and average consultation time.
The system shall list departments and the doctors belonging to each department.
The system shall show the free appointment slots of a doctor for a selected date, based on working days, working hours, slot length and existing bookings.
The Receptionist shall be able to book an appointment for a registered patient with a doctor in a free slot that is not in the past and lies within the doctor's working hours.
The system shall reject a booking that overlaps an existing active appointment of the same doctor or of the same patient.
The Receptionist shall be able to reschedule an appointment while it is in the SCHEDULED state, subject to the same slot rules.
The Receptionist shall be able to cancel a SCHEDULED appointment with a mandatory reason; the freed slot becomes bookable again.
The system shall list appointments filtered by date, doctor and status.
On check-in of a SCHEDULED appointment for today, the system shall issue a queue token unique per doctor per day and set the appointment state to CHECKED_IN.
The system shall display a live queue board per doctor showing waiting, in-consultation and served patients, ordered by priority (URGENT first) and then check-in time.
The system shall estimate each waiting patient's waiting time as (patients ahead × doctor's average consultation time) + remaining time of the consultation in progress.
Receptionists, Doctors and Administrators shall be able to mark a waiting patient URGENT with a mandatory reason; the action shall be audited.
A Doctor shall be able to call the next patient from their queue only when no consultation of theirs is in progress; the appointment moves to IN_CONSULTATION.
A Doctor shall be able to record a consultation for an appointment in IN_CONSULTATION: symptoms, vitals, diagnosis, clinical notes and optional follow-up date; diagnosis is required to complete it.
A Doctor shall be able to issue a prescription of one or more medicines with dosage, frequency, duration and quantity (> 0) during a consultation.
A Doctor shall be able to order one or more lab tests for a patient during a consultation or an admission.
Completing a consultation shall set the appointment to COMPLETED and add the doctor's consultation fee as an unbilled charge.
Only clinical roles (Doctor, Administrator) shall view diagnoses and clinical notes; Receptionist and Billing Staff shall be denied.
The Lab Technician shall see a worklist of lab orders filtered by status (ORDERED, SAMPLE_COLLECTED, COMPLETED, CANCELLED).
The Lab Technician shall record sample collection (ORDERED → SAMPLE_COLLECTED) and then enter the result (SAMPLE_COLLECTED → COMPLETED); other transitions shall be rejected.
The system shall automatically flag a numeric result outside the test's reference range as ABNORMAL.
Ordering a lab test shall add the test price as an unbilled charge; cancelling an ORDERED test shall remove the unbilled charge.
The Pharmacist shall manage the medicine inventory: add medicines, restock quantities and record batch and expiry date.
The system shall raise alerts for medicines at or below their reorder level and for medicines expiring within 30 days or already expired.
The Pharmacist shall dispense a PENDING prescription only if every item is in stock and not expired; dispensing reduces stock and adds medicine charges.
The system shall show a ward-wise bed board with each bed's status: AVAILABLE, RESERVED, OCCUPIED, CLEANING or MAINTENANCE.
The Receptionist shall admit a patient to an AVAILABLE bed; a patient may have only one active admission and a bed may hold only one patient.
The Receptionist shall transfer an admitted patient to another AVAILABLE bed; the previous bed moves to CLEANING and bed charges are kept per stay.
Bed status changes shall follow the bed state machine (AVAILABLE→RESERVED→OCCUPIED→CLEANING→AVAILABLE, AVAILABLE↔MAINTENANCE, RESERVED→AVAILABLE); invalid transitions shall be rejected.
A Doctor shall request discharge with a discharge summary (ADMITTED → DISCHARGE_PENDING); bed charges (days × daily rate, minimum 1 day) are then added as unbilled charges.
Discharge shall be completed only when all charges of the admission are invoiced and fully paid, unless an Administrator overrides with a recorded reason; the bed then moves to CLEANING.
Billing Staff shall generate an invoice for a patient from all of that patient's unbilled charges (consultation, lab, medicine, bed), with a unique invoice number.
Billing Staff shall be able to apply a discount of 0–50% with a reason to an UNPAID invoice.
Billing Staff shall record full or partial payments (Cash, Card, UPI); a payment must be greater than zero and not exceed the outstanding balance. Invoice status moves UNPAID → PARTIALLY_PAID → PAID.
The system shall generate a printable receipt with a unique receipt number for every payment and a printable invoice.
The dashboard shall show today's KPIs: appointments, patients waiting, bed occupancy, revenue collected, pending lab orders and stock alerts.
The Administrator shall view reports for a date range: appointments per day and status, revenue per day and payment method, bed occupancy per ward and top diagnoses.

The system shall record an append-only audit entry (user, role, action, entity, entity id, timestamp, summary) for every create, update and state change, without storing passwords; Administrators can search it.

nonFunctional.text: 95% of API requests shall complete within 500 ms on a standard laptop with the demo dataset; pages shall render within 2 seconds.
Passwords shall be stored only as bcrypt hashes; all API routes except login shall require a signed JWT; all SQL shall use parameterised statements.
Access to clinical data shall follow the principle of least privilege defined in the role-permission matrix; audit logs shall not contain passwords or tokens.
Multi-step operations (admission + bed update, dispensing + stock update, invoice generation, payment recording) shall execute in a single database transaction.
The interface shall be responsive (≥ 360 px width), use consistent colour-coded status badges, show field-level validation messages and allow booking an appointment in at most 4 steps.
The code shall follow a layered architecture (UI → REST API → Services → Domain rules → Data access); business rules shall be isolated in pure, unit-tested domain modules.
The system shall run on Windows, macOS and Linux with Node.js 20 or later, and on current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari browsers.
Every state-changing operation shall be traceable to an authenticated user and timestamp through the audit trail.
The production deployment should target 99.5% availability during hospital operating hours, with daily database backups (out of scope for the prototype).
The design shall support at least 50 concurrent staff users and 100,000 patient records without architectural change.

businessRules.text: Patient ID format is P followed by 5 digits, assigned sequentially and never reused.
Appointment slots start at the doctor's work start time and repeat every slot length until work end; bookings must align to a slot boundary.
Active appointment states are SCHEDULED, CHECKED_IN and IN_CONSULTATION; only these block a slot.
Appointment life cycle: SCHEDULED → CHECKED_IN → IN_CONSULTATION → COMPLETED; SCHEDULED → CANCELLED; SCHEDULED → NO_SHOW.
Queue order: URGENT before NORMAL, then earlier check-in first. Wait estimate = ahead × average consultation minutes + max(average − elapsed, 1) when a consultation is in progress.
Lab order life cycle: ORDERED → SAMPLE_COLLECTED → COMPLETED; ORDERED → CANCELLED.
Low stock when quantity ≤ reorder level; near-expiry when expiry is within 30 days; expired medicines cannot be dispensed.

Bed state machine: AVAILABLE→RESERVED, AVAILABLE→OCCUPIED, AVAILABLE→MAINTENANCE, RESERVED→OCCUPIED, RESERVED→AVAILABLE, OCCUPIED→CLEANING, CLEANING→AVAILABLE, CLEANING→MAINTENANCE, MAINTENANCE→AVAILABLE.
Admission life cycle: ADMITTED → DISCHARGE_PENDING → DISCHARGED. Bed days = ceil(hours stayed / 24), minimum 1, charged at the ward's daily rate per stay.
Invoice life cycle: UNPAID → PARTIALLY_PAID → PAID; UNPAID → CANCELLED (only when no payment exists). Discount 0–50% only while UNPAID.
Payments: amount > 0 and ≤ outstanding balance; methods CASH, CARD, UPI; receipt number R-YYYYMMDD-NNNN.
Account lockout: 5 consecutive failures lock the account for 15 minutes; a successful login resets the counter.
